papers.title: Respons Mahasiswa STAB Kertarajasa Terhadap Praktik Meditasi Vipassana di Padepokan Dhammadipa Arama
papers.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui respon mahasiswa STAB Kertarajasa terhadap praktik meditasi vipassana di Padepokan Dhammadipa Arama. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif dengan subjek penelitian sebanyak 25 mahasiswa semester 6 dan 8. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui angket dengan indikator: konsistensi, tingkat kesulitan, manfaat, dan kepuasan terhadap meditasi. Analisis dilakukan dengan menggunakan skala likert. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa secara keseluruhan respon mahasiswa terhadap praktik meditasi vipassana berada pada kategori “berat” sebesar 77%. Indikator konsistensi memperoleh skor tertinggi pada kategori “sangat berat” (84%), diikuti oleh tingkat kesulitan (73%), manfaat (76%), dan kepuasan (72%). Temuan tersebut menunjukkan bahwa meskipun mahasiswa menyadari manfaat dari praktik meditasi, mereka menghadapi tantangan besar dalam hal konsistensi dan kepuasan selama proses meditasi. Oleh karena itu, perlu adanya evaluasi dan penyesuaian dalam pelaksanaan program meditasi agar lebih sesuai dengan kebutuhan dan kondisi mahasiswa.

papers.title: Satva Bala and Vipassana Meditation in Young Adults Conceptual Foundations Evidence and Research Priorities
papers.abstract:
Background : Satva Bala is an Ayurvedic account of
mental strength expressed through steadiness, judgment,
memory, purposeful conduct, courage, and tolerance of
adversity. Vipassana is an intensive contemplative practice
centred on ethical restraint, sustained attention, awareness
of bodily sensations, and nonreactivity. The two traditions
use different conceptual languages, yet several functional
domains overlap.
Objective To examine the conceptual relationship between
Satva Bala and Vipassana meditation, summarize relevant
contemporary evidence, and define a rigorous research
agenda for young adults.
Methods A focused narrative review integrated classical
Ayurvedic sources with peer reviewed studies and
systematic reviews indexed in PubMed through September
2026. Literature on Vipassana, traditional meditation
retreats, mindfulness mechanisms, resilience, cognition,
psychophysiology, measurement, and adverse experiences
was prioritized. Because the review was interpretive rather
than systematic, no pooled estimate or formal risk of bias
score was produced.
Synthesis Vipassana may plausibly engage attention
regulation, interoceptive awareness, decentering, response
inhibition, emotional recovery, and prosocial orientation.
These functions resemble parts of the Satva Bala profile but
are not equivalent to it. Retreat and mindfulness studies
report potential benefits for distress, well-being, cognitive
control, and selected physiological measures; however,
heterogeneity, self selection, weak control conditions,
inconsistent definitions, and underreporting of adverse
experiences limit causal interpretation. The available Satva
Bala questionnaire also needs modern psychometric
evaluation.
Conclusion Vipassana provides a defensible hypothesis for
strengthening selected expressions of Satva Bala, not proof
that the classical construct and modern psychological
measures are interchangeable. Future research should
preserve the integrity of both knowledge systems, measure
mechanisms directly, use credible controls, report harms,
and validate the Ayurveda specific outcome before testing
efficacy.

papers.title: Changes in Mindful Technology Use and Digital Well-Being Following a Vipassana Mindfulness Program: An Exploratory Case Study of College Students
papers.abstract: The present study examined the changes in mindful technology use and digital well-being following a four-week Vipassana meditation training program among college students. A pretest and posttest case study design was used with one male and one female college student from Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. Participants spent more than five hours a day using digital devices and reported mild digital fatigue, distraction, and emotional strain. Before and after the programme, the study variables were measured through the Digital Well-Being Scale (DWS) and Mindful Technology Use Inventory (MTUI-32). The male participant’s digital well-being score increased from 58 to 72, while the female participant’s score increased from 61 to 76. Scores for mindful technology use increased from 45 to 63 for the male participant and from 68 to 81 for the female participant. The findings from weekly reflection journals suggested perceived changes in attention, emotional balance, and responses to digital distractions. These results are preliminary and cannot be generalised because the sample was small and there was no control group; the observed changes cannot be attributed specifically to Vipassana meditation.

papers.title: Assessment of Satva Bala Following Ten-Days Residential Vipassana Course in Young Adults: A Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study Protocol
papers.abstract:
Background : Satva Bala describes the functional strength
and steadiness of the mind in Ayurveda. A structured
residential Vipassana course combines ethical discipline,
sustained attention to respiration and bodily sensations,
equanimous observation, silence, and a regulated daily
routine. These components may influence several capacities
represented in Satva Bala, but direct longitudinal evidence
is limited.
Objective: To estimate immediate and three-month changes
in Satva Bala among first time young adult participants
completing a standard ten-day residential Vipassana
course.
Methods : This prospective single cohort study will recruit
250 adults aged 18 to 40 years at Dhamma Punna
Vipassana Meditation Centre in Pune. Participants with a
diagnosed major mental disorder, major physical illness,
ongoing psychiatric treatment or psychotropic medication,
or previous completion of a ten day Vipassana course will
be excluded. The primary outcome is change in the 14 item
Ayurveda derived Satva Bala questionnaire score from
baseline to course completion. Monthly assessments will
continue for three months. Pulse and blood pressure will be
recorded before and after the residential course. The main
analysis will use a linear mixed effects model with time as a
categorical fixed effect and participant as a random
intercept. Adjusted mean changes, 95 percent confidence
intervals, standardized effect sizes, score distributions,
category transitions, missing data, and adverse experiences
will be reported.
Interpretation: The design can describe within person
change and its persistence but cannot isolate a causal effect
of meditation from self selection, expectancy, the retreat
environment, silence, diet, sleep schedule, or other
concurrent features. The study is intended to generate a
transparent estimate and inform a later controlled trial and
psychometric validation of the questionnaire.

papers.title: VIPASSANĀ AS LIVED RELIGION
papers.abstract: This article examines a 14-day Mahasi vipassanā (insight meditation) retreat in Yangon, Myanmar, as a form of lived religion. It aims to analyze how non-self (anattā) emerges in meditative practice as an experiential process and to assess the value of self-ethnography for the study of contemplative practice. The analysis is based on self-ethnographic notes and recordings produced during the retreat and later analyzed retrospectively. Although the retreat took place across two centers—Mahasi Sāsana Yeiktha and Panditarama—it is treated as a continuous contemplative process, since both followed the same Mahasi method. Organized in three phases, the analysis traces a movement from initial doubt and adjustment, through pain, equanimity, and concentration, to more explicit experiences of impermanence, attachment, and the destabilization of the self. The results show that non-self emerges not merely as a doctrinal concept, but as an experiential weakening of ownership, control, and fixed identity. The article also argues that self-ethnography is a productive method for examining how contemplative practice is bodily enacted, interpretively shaped, and lived as religion, while requiring reflexive care regarding the relation between experience and interpretation.

papers.title: Interventions to reduce perinatal suicidality: a global systematic review.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Perinatal suicidality (suicidal thoughts, behaviours, plans and attempts) is a risk factor for suicide. Evidence on interventions to reduce perinatal suicidality remains limited. This systematic review examined the effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions to reduce suicidality in perinatal women. METHODS: This review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251081528). Seven databases were searched from 2010 to December 2025. Interventions assessing a reduction in perinatal suicidality as a primary, secondary, or safety monitoring outcome were included. Two reviewers independently screened articles. A narrative summary was compiled. Risk of bias was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. RESULTS: Six studies were included: 5 randomised controlled trials (3 individually randomised, 1 cluster, 1 noninferiority) and 1 historical controlled trial. Three studies investigated suicidality as a primary or secondary outcome, and three studies collected suicidality data for safety monitoring. Of these, two investigated multidisciplinary community health programmes, and one evaluated a behavioural activation therapy. Two studies showed a reduction in suicidality, and one showed a significant reduction at 3-4 months postpartum, but not at 7-8 months. Three studies assessed suicidality as safety monitoring. These studies investigated eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing therapy, a practice-level intervention incorporated into obstetric practices, and an electronic mindfulness-based intervention. These studies were not adequately powered to assess a reduction in suicidality. DISCUSSION: Few studies have investigated suicidality as a primary or secondary outcome. Although some health system level and psychological interventions were associated with a reduction in suicidality, robust evidence from interventions specifically designed to reduce perinatal suicidality is needed.

From Quantum Brain to Quantum Mind: The Ontological Promotion Gap in Quantum-Biological Theories of Consciousness.
papers.abstract: Quantum effects in biological systems are increasingly investigated at molecular, cellular, and neural scales, yet evidence for quantum organization in a living brain does not by itself determine the ontological status of the conscious states realized by that brain. This article distinguishes seven claims often compressed under "quantum consciousness": quantum occurrence, causal relevance, constitutive relevance, phenomenal bridging, phenomenal individuation, quantum mental status, and quantum-formal adequacy. It argues that evidence for the first three-even if decisive-does not by itself establish quantum mental status. I call this cross-level inferential discontinuity the Ontological Promotion Gap. The argument is developed in relation to current quantum-biological approaches to consciousness, including hierarchical microtubule models, nuclear-spin mechanisms, non-classical neuroimaging, dissipative quantum-brain models, autopoietic quantum constraints, and quantum-like cognition. Drawing on multilevel biological organization and contemporary neurophenomenology, the paper introduces a Phenomenal Individuation Condition: for a conscious state to be non-trivially quantum, quantum-specific structure must contribute to the organization or counterfactual differentiation of the phenomenal state itself, rather than merely occur within its biological realization. Quantum-like cognition supplies the converse dissociation: quantum formalism can characterize cognition without establishing quantum physical implementation. The resulting framework yields a Level-Specific Quantum Attribution Principle and an explicit experimental decision structure for determining what different classes of quantum-biological evidence do-and do not-license us to conclude about a quantum mind.

papers.title: Social Bonds as Predictors of a Central Symptom of Problematic Short-Form Video Use Across Genders: A Network Analysis and Machine Learning Study.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Problematic short-form video use (PSVU) has emerged as a pressing public health issue. Although research on this topic is expanding, few studies have systematically explored the complex predictors of problematic short-form video use across genders. This study sought to combine network analysis and machine learning (ML) to decode the associations between social bonds and problematic short-form video use across genders. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey of 2076 Chinese adolescents (51.73% girls, mean age = 13.75) assessed problematic short-form video use, social bonds (attachment, commitment, involvement, belief), and demographic information. RESULTS: Results indicated that PSVU2 (i.e., increasing time for satisfaction) was the central symptom of problematic short-form video use across genders. ML findings revealed that commitment was the most predictive dimension for the central symptom of problematic short-form video use in both boys and girls, followed by belief, involvement, attachment, and demographic information at the dimension level. At the factor level, the top six factors with the greatest predictive contributions in girls were academic engagement, prosocial behaviors, mindfulness, responsibility, belief in a just world, and grit. In boys, these factors were responsibility, academic engagement, mindfulness, grit, parent-child relationships, and belief in a just world. CONCLUSIONS: These findings offer both theoretical insights and practical guidance for intervention strategies targeting adolescent problematic short-form video use.

papers.title: Psychosocial interventions for adolescent substance use and related outcomes: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: This systematic review synthesized evidence on the effectiveness of psychosocial interventions for reducing adolescent substance use and improving related psychiatric and psychosocial outcomes. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261284775) on January 14, 2026. The review was conducted between November 13, 2025, and February 14, 2026, and searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science for randomized controlled trials published between January 2015 and December 2025. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. RESULTS: Thirty-four RCTs were included. Cognitive-behavioral and motivational approaches were the most frequently investigated interventions (29.41 % and 32.35 % of studies, respectively), although their comparative superiority could not be established. Selected trials reported favorable effects on substance use outcomes, including reduced odds of substance use disorder following a personality-targeted cognitive-behavioral intervention (OR = 0.66, 95 % CI: 0.46-0.92) and reduced smoking initiation following a school-based intervention (OR = 0.65, 95 % CI: 0.44-0.97). However, findings were mixed: a digital intervention showed no significant effect on smoking (OR = 1.01, 95 % CI: 0.62-1.66), and a mindfulness-based intervention showed no advantage over usual treatment in reducing cannabis use (d = 0.02, p = 0.930). Other interventions showed benefits restricted to specific outcomes, subgroups, or follow-up periods. Risk-of-bias assessments identified some concerns in 20 studies (58.82 %) and high risk in 14 (41.18 %). CONCLUSIONS: Psychosocial interventions may improve selected adolescent substance use outcomes, but findings are heterogeneous and frequently include non-significant or time-limited effects. Methodological limitations, variability in outcome measures, and the absence of a pooled quantitative synthesis prevent firm conclusions regarding comparative effectiveness and clinical significance.

papers.title: Practicing Focused Attention or Open Monitoring During Interoceptive Challenges: Seed-Based Functional Connectivity Changes Following Video-Based Online MBSR.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) has been shown to improve well-being, but its neural mechanisms during interoceptive challenges remain unclear, particularly when delivered online. Previous neuroimaging research has primarily focused on the salience network, with limited attention to the dorsal attention network. This study investigated changes in functional connectivity within these networks following an eight-week video-based online MBSR program. METHODS: Thirty-nine healthy adults were included in the analysis (18 in the MBSR group and 21 in the control group). Participants underwent functional MRI before and after the intervention, while experiencing intermittent inspiratory occlusions under baseline, focused attention (FA), and open monitoring (OM) conditions. Seed-based connectivity analyses used bilateral frontal eye fields and anterior cingulate cortices as seeds for the dorsal attention and salience networks, respectively. RESULTS: Exploratory analysis revealed a significant Group × Time interaction in anterior cingulate seed connectivity during OM. This finding survived correction within the seed-by-condition map but not across all six interaction analyses. Connectivity with the right frontal pole showed a greater negative change in the MBSR group than in the control group. Within the MBSR group, frontal eye field connectivity changed with frontal and occipital regions during FA. Anterior cingulate connectivity also changed in frontal, sensorimotor, parietal, and occipital regions during FA and with the left frontal pole during OM. In the control group, the only significant change was increased frontal eye field connectivity with the right temporal fusiform cortex during OM. CONCLUSIONS: Functional connectivity between the network seeds and specific cortical regions changed following video-based online MBSR. Exploratory analysis also identified a group difference in connectivity changes between the anterior cingulate cortex and the right frontal pole during OM, although this finding requires replication. The functional significance of these neural changes for behavioral outcomes, including interoceptive awareness and attentional regulation, warrants further investigation.
